hint.text: Adages and proverbs use figurative language to express a widely accepted statement about life.
hint.label: Adages & Proverbs

instruction.text: Match the adages and proverbs with their meaning.

atoms.a: the early bird catches the worm
atoms.b: someone who starts early will be successful
obsessing about something will only cause time to pass slowly

atoms.a: you can’t make a cake without breaking eggs
atoms.b: it is inevitable and important for mistakes to happen

atoms.a: absence makes the heart grow fonder
atoms.b: when you take space from a loved one you become more affectionate

instruction.text: Match the adages and proverbs with their meaning.

atoms.a: Don’t judge a book by its cover
atoms.b: you shouldn’t assume things about someone or something by just appearances
the things you do show more of how you feel than what you say
it is wiser to be cautious and take your time with things than to rush into things that you may regret in the future

instruction.text: Read the scenario and then choose the adage or proverb that fits.

atoms.a: Sam is upset because her boyfriend is going on holiday with his family for 5 weeks.
Alonzo doesn’t think the new student is cool because they’re wearing silly shoes.
Dafydd always wears a helmet when he cycles to school.
Mack is anxiously staring at the clock waiting until the right time to pick up their girlfriend from the airport.
